properties.Name: Upper White River Outwash
properties.Region_Description: Relatively flat at around 750 ft of elevation, with some stream valleys. It is bounded by the White Lick Creek to the west and the White River to the south and east. It is covered by loam till, with outwash and alluvium along the streams. 19 high-capacity wells operate in the outwash deposits, ranging from 300-4800 GPM and averaging 2000 GPM. This region includes the township of Brooklyn.

properties.Name: Mill Creek Till Plain
properties.Region_Description: Exhibits flat terrain transitioning to rolling hills in the south beyond the glacial boundary line. Silt and till covers the siltstone Borden bedrock. A buried bedrock valley runs along the modern Mud Creek that allows some aquifer availability in this region, but generally less than 10 GPM of water can be developed. There are no high-capacity wells or townships in this region. Several karst features have developed along the southern side of the region and the transition between the Tipton Till and Morgan Hills.

properties.Name: Highland Creek Hills
properties.Region_Description: This region is very hilly, with a relief of 245 ft. It is bounded by siltstone and shale hills to the east, and sandy loam and till to the west. No high-capacity wells are in this region due to most of the unconsolidated sediment being till. The west side of Brooklyn Township is on the eastern border of this region. Several karst features have developed along the transition between the Tipton Till and Morgan Hills.

properties.Name: South Morgan Upland
properties.Region_Description: This region makes up the southern edge of the county and is bounded by the alluvial floodplains of the White River to the north. The region is distinguishable from surrounding regions by high hilly relief of 143 ft with lots of drainageways. The lithology of the area is mainly exposed Borden siltstone and shale with areas of sandy loam and terra rosa in the southwest corner of the county. No townships or high-capacity wells are in this region.

properties.Name: Lower White River Outwash
properties.Region_Description: This region is the most uniform of the regions, marked by the alluvium and outwash in the White River flood plain. Three high-capacity wells operate in the area: 100 GPM is produced in Paragon Township; 2500 GPM is produced in the two wells on the eastern side of the region.

properties.Name: Indian Creek Hills
properties.Region_Description: This hilly region is marked by a hilly relief of 179 ft, with a high elevation of 950 ft. It is bounded by hilly till to the north, outwash to the northwest, and Indian Creek to the south. In addition to the till, a region of exposed shale bedrock appears in the center of the region along ridgetops and alluvium deposits along Indian Creek. 15 high-capacity wells operate in the region, ranging from 50 GPM in the outwash to 1000 GPM in alluvial sediment. The Morgantown Township is in this region.

properties.Name: Scotts Creek Till Plain
properties.Region_Description: This region is bounded by the White River floodplain to the north and the Morgantown Hills to the south. It exhibits high and flat till plains, with some outwash along Stotts Creek. There are no high-capacity wells or townships in this area.

properties.Name: Middle White River Outwash
properties.Region_Description: This region is hilly, ranging from 550-950 ft of elevation with more relief to the west and more rolling hills to the east. This region has the thickest amount of unconsolidated material over bedrock, with mostly outwash, alluvium, and drift. A portion shale bedrock is exposed in the middle of this region. 43 high-capacity wells operate in the region ranging from 170 GPM in till areas to 1400 GPM in outwash along the White River. This region includes the township of Martinsville.

properties.Name: White Lick Till Plain
properties.Region_Description: This region is bounded on the southeast side by White Lick Creek, including the entirety of Mooresville. Till, alluvium, and outwash is deposited along the creek to the east of the region. 17 high-capacity wells operate in the outwash system, ranging from 100-1000 GPM. This region also includes the township of Monrovia.
